summary.text: Grossi is a nurse and retired U.S. Army colonel running as the Republican nominee. According to his campaign website, he grew up in a Cambridge public housing project, served 29 years in the Army and Army Reserve including a deployment to Iraq, and worked as a nurse at VA medical centers. His campaign website lists affordability, public safety, government transparency and term limits among his priorities.

paragraphs.text: Born and raised in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in the Corcoran Park housing project, and graduated from Cambridge High and Latin in 1977, according to his campaign website.
Before nursing school, managed restaurants in Harvard Square and worked in mental health at Metropolitan State Hospital, according to his campaign website.
Earned a bachelor's degree in nursing from UMass Boston.

Served 29 years in the U.S. Army and Army Reserve, according to his campaign website, including as clinical team leader at Walter Reed Army Medical Center, mobilization officer with combat support hospital units, a 2006-2007 deployment to Mosul and Al Asad, Iraq, and Deputy Commander for Nursing Services (colonel) of the 399th Combat Support Hospital from 2007 to 2019.

Worked as a psychiatric nurse at the West Palm Beach VA Medical Center (1995-2000) and in outpatient substance-abuse and psychiatry at the Bedford VA Hospital (2000-2022), and also did community-based substance-abuse and psychiatric care at Choate Hospital in Woburn, per his campaign website.
Received write-in votes in the 2024 Republican primary for the Massachusetts House of Representatives 37th Middlesex District; no candidate advanced from that primary.
Lists himself as vice chair of the Acton Republican Town Committee and a board member of Iron Works Farm, and says he is married with two children, according to his campaign website.
